correctness.rationale: For every D,L,kappa>0, 0<x<L, the solved backward joint Laplace BVP gives the normalized transform as a product of the conditional two-absorbing-endpoint hitting transform and (kappa+D/L)/(kappa+sqrt(Ds)coth(L sqrt(s/D))). The coth partial fraction is a Bernstein exponent with an explicit infinite-activity finite-mean Levy measure, yielding an independent subordinator-at-exponential delay and a strictly ordered pathwise coupling. A Sturm-Liouville Robin/Dirichlet canonical product yields independent Bernoulli-exponential summands, whose positive expectation sum converges. Root interlacing and the n^-3 sum yield uniform W1 error <=2L^2/(D pi^2 N^2). Differentiation yields stated mean/variance and weak-kappa limit. The included check.py completed 30 positive-parameter transform, truncated-product and moment consistency tests. No sample-only inference of infinite statements.

value.rationale: The source explicitly distinguishes capture probability from conditional completion time in endocytosis-motivated diffusion. This result upgrades the expectation to an exact distribution, proves an unambiguous all-quantile stochastic monotonicity despite success-conditioning, quantifies the finite weak-reactivity conditional time when success itself becomes rare, and provides a practical finite-sum sampler with rate-uniform Wasserstein error. These structural properties are not mean-only calculations or arbitrary model slices; the flat interval is a natural controlled limiting benchmark for a known heterogeneous model.
